paper.title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of a Peer Growth Group Intervention to Enhance Psychological Resilience in Early Career Nurses: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
paper.summary:
BACKGROUND: Early career nurses face significant occupational pressures and risks, making psychological resilience critical for effective management of workplace stress. This study evaluated the effectiveness of a theory-driven resilience-building intervention for early career nurses.
METHOD: This study adopted a two-arm, 1:1 pilot randomized controlled trial design to evaluate the effectiveness of a bi-weekly, eight-session resilience intervention for early career nurses. Outcome was measured by the Nurse Resilience Scale, Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale, and general self-efficacy scale.
RESULTS: Twenty-seven nurses were randomly assigned to an intervention group (n = 13) or a wait-list control group (n = 14). The intervention significantly improved overall nurse resilience (p = .016), and no significant between-group differences were found in self-efficacy (overall p = .98).
CONCLUSION: The findings demonstrate that a structured, theory-driven intervention can effectively enhance resilience among early career nurses, which highlights the intervention's practical utility in fostering adaptive coping mechanisms.

paper.title: Chronic neonatal MK-801 treatment attenuates auditory fear conditioning in adult male rats.
paper.summary: Noncompetitive-777-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor antagonists induce schizophrenia-like symptoms, supporting the NMDA receptor hypofunction hypothesis. Neonatal NMDA receptor blockade with MK-801 is widely used to model neurodevelopmental aspects of schizophrenia; however, its impact on cue-specific fear learning remains incompletely characterized. Male Sprague-Dawley pups received subcutaneous injections of MK-801 (0.4 mg/kg) or saline twice daily from postnatal day 7-20. In adulthood, rats underwent auditory fear conditioning (five tone-shock pairings), 4 days of extinction (45 tone-alone trials/session), a retrieval test, and a remote retrieval test. Across acquisition and all test sessions, MK-801-treated rats showed consistently lower freezing than controls. These findings suggest that chronic neonatal MK-801 treatment disrupts acquisition or expression of cue-shock associations, or both. Given the small sample size and the potential contribution of altered locomotion or shock reactivity, future work should incorporate locomotor and sensory controls.

paper.title: A Multimodal Hyaluronic Acid Approach to Compensate Menopause-Related Skin Changes: Hyaluronic Acid Serum Subanalysis With HA Filler Injection.
paper.summary:
BACKGROUND: Estrogen depletion during menopause reduces collagen, elastin, and glycosaminoglycans (GAG) synthesis, particularly hyaluronic acid (HA), and is associated with skin thinness, wrinkles, reduced elasticity, and decreased hydration.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy of an integrated facial antiaging approach using a multiglycan HA serum with HA filler injection in menopausal women.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A serum formulation (containing HA, dipotassium glycyrrhizate, purple rice extract, Lactobacillus/soybean ferment extract, pro-Xylane) was applied twice daily on the face from Day -14 to Day 56 and integrated with nasolabial fold HA dermal filler injection on Day 0. In a post hoc subanalysis of 12 menopausal women, facial aging signs were assessed using instrumental measurements of skin elasticity and firmness, and standardized photography.
RESULTS: At baseline, net skin elasticity in the temple area and in the nasolabial fold area were lower in the menopausal subgroup compared with the overall cohort. In menopausal women, nasolabial and temple skin elasticity showed improvement between baseline and Day 56.
CONCLUSION: A multimodal HA serum integrated with HA dermal injection may offer a promising facial rejuvenation strategy in menopausal women with skin aging signs.

paper.title: Osteopathic manipulative treatment in resolving post-stroke depression: a case report.
paper.summary: Depression affects approximately one in three people following a stroke, most commonly within the first year. The current standard of care for post-stroke depression (PSD) does not differ from that of a non-stroke patient. Few studies have investigated the application of osteopathic manipulative treatment (OMT) within psychiatric conditions; however, studies have demonstrated its potential in downregulating the body's stress response. In this case report, we explore the use of OMT as an adjunct intervention for new-onset mild depressive symptoms following a stroke. This case follows a 64-year-old woman who presented to an outpatient behavioral health clinic in October 2024 for depressed mood following a left middle cerebral artery stroke four months prior. She initiated psychotherapy and declined medication management. After four months of psychotherapy exclusively, her mood symptoms continued to worsen and her PHQ-9 was 7. In April 2025, after six months of psychotherapy, she began OMT every two weeks, for a total of three treatments, addressing somatic dysfunctions of the head, cervical spine, thoracic inlet, and associated musculature. At each session, she completed the PHQ-9 and a pre- and post-session questionnaire assessing specific mood symptoms (sleep, irritability, stress/tension, hopelessness, anxious mood, and depressed mood). At initiation of OMT, the patient's PHQ-9 score was 5, with clinician-observed emotional lability and tearfulness. Her pre-session questionnaire indicated disturbances in sleep, irritability, hopelessness, and depressed mood. Immediately following her first treatment, the patient noted absence of symptoms on post-OMT questionnaire. Following three OMT sessions, her PHQ-9 decreased to 0 and there was no self-reported anxious or depressed mood, irritability, or hopelessness. After two months without OMT, the patient's depressive symptoms and emotional lability returned. These symptoms resolved immediately following an additional OMT session. Two weeks later, her PHQ-9 was 0 and no other mood symptoms were reported. With ongoing OMT every 4-6 weeks, subsequent PHQ-9's continued to be 0. This case suggests the potential of integrating OMT in the treatment of mild PSD, with this patient experiencing initial resolution of depressive symptoms following three OMT sessions. We hope these findings encourage providers to consider OMT in management of depressive symptoms following stroke and spur further investigation of the utilization of OMT as an adjunctive treatment in PSD.

paper.title: Vocal and musical emotion perception, voice cue discrimination, and quality of life in cochlear implant users with and without acoustic hearing
paper.summary: This study aims to provide a comprehensive picture of auditory emotion perception in cochlear implant (CI) users by (1) investigating emotion categorisation in both vocal (pseudo-speech) and musical domains and (2) how individual differences in residual acoustic hearing, sensitivity to voice cues (voice pitch, vocal tract length), and quality of life (QoL) might be associated with vocal emotion perception and, going a step further, also with musical emotion perception. In 28 adult CI users, with or without self-reported acoustic hearing, we showed that sensitivity (d’) scores for emotion categorisation varied largely across the participants, in line with previous research. However, within participants, the d’ scores for vocal and musical emotion categorisation were significantly correlated, indicating both similar processing of auditory emotional cues across the pseudo-speech and music domains as well as robustness of the tests. Only for musical emotion perception, emotion d’ scores were higher in implant users with residual acoustic hearing compared to no acoustic hearing. The voice pitch perception did not significantly correlate with emotion categorisation in either domain, while the vocal tract length significantly correlated in both domains. For QoL, only the sub-domain of Speech production ability, but not the overall QoL scores, correlated with vocal emotion categorisation, partially supporting previous findings. Taken together, results indicate that auditory emotion perception is challenging for some CI users, possibly a consequence of how available the emotion-related cues are via electric hearing. Improving these cues, either via rehabilitation or training, may also help auditory emotion perception in CI users.
